page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c4g1.xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance belonging to the ecs.gn5 family. It is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server features 30.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.5 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA Pascal P100 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 472 GB SSD, and network connectivity is supported by a 3 Gbps baseline bandwidth under a KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals a significant performance divergence between the host CPU/memory subsystem and the GPU accelerator. The Intel Xeon CPU scores in the bottom 10% for stress-ng single-core performance and the bottom 25% for multi-core performance. Memory bandwidth is similarly limited, with large block read and write speeds falling into the bottom 10% tier. However, the onboard NVIDIA P100 GPU delivers top-tier results for LLM inference. Prompt processing for a 7B model reaches 316.25 tokens per second, and text generation achieves 42.76 tokens per second, both placing in the top 10% of benchmarks.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents an entry-level GPU tier where users trade off host CPU processing power and memory speed to gain access to dedicated hardware acceleration. The inclusion of a 472 GB local SSD provides a localized storage buffer for model weights or datasets. This hardware profile is suited for GPU-bound workloads such as small-to-medium LLM inference, machine learning model evaluation, and basic parallel processing tasks that do not heavily rely on host CPU performance or high memory throughput.
